core_obligations: Prove that approximation holds for every triple (T, E, m) over an algebraic space representable by an affine scheme, provided E is m-pseudo-coherent, H^i(E) is supported on T for i >= m - r + 1, and X minus T is a union of r affine opens; in particular approximation by perfect complexes holds for affine schemes
proof_roadmap: Represent X by the affine scheme X0 and write E = epsilon^*E0 by the comparison lemma; E0 is m-pseudo-coherent by descent of pseudo-coherence.
Comparing stalks shows H^i(E0) is supported on the corresponding closed subset T0 for i >= m - r + 1.
The scheme approximation lemma produces an approximation P0 -> E0 of (T0, E0, m); pulling back along epsilon and using descent of perfectness yields the approximation P = epsilon^*P_0 -> E on X.
difficulty_reason: H3: a comparison-and-descent argument transporting the affine scheme approximation theorem to the etale site.
